items.title: Stage - Marketing Turf F/H
items.description: WE ARE BETCLIC 🎯 Betclic, leader européen des paris sportifs, est bien plus qu'un simple site de jeux en ligne ! Présente dans plusieurs pays et sur différents continents avec une offre incluant également le poker, les paris hippiques et les jeux de casino, notre entreprise se distingue par son esprit inspirant et tourné vers l'avenir : chaque journée y apporte son lot de nouveaux défis, au sein d'un environnement moderne et dynamique. Acteur majeur du secteur technologique affichant une croissance forte et soutenue, nous croyons en l'innovation portée par la diversité et l'inclusion, et encourageons chacun à exprimer tout son potentiel. Grâce à nos équipes multiculturelles, nous proposons une expérience de jeu optimale, sûre et responsable, s'appuyant sur des technologies de pointe. WHY JOIN US? 🚀 Chez Betclic, la réussite repose sur des équipes passionnées et engagées. Voici pourquoi vous aimerez travailler avec nous : 💡 Un environnement international et créatif où chaque projet est une opportunité d'innover 📈 Une hypercroissance synonyme de nouveaux défis et d'opportunités de développement au quotidien 🏡 Un équilibre vie pro/vie perso préservé : vous pouvez télétravailler jusqu'à 3 jours par semaine et profiter de bureaux exceptionnels. 🌟 Une ambiance unique et conviviale, avec 1 600 collaborateurs répartis dans 5 pays et un siège social basé à Bordeaux Vous êtes passionné(e) de sport et de technologie ? Rejoignez-nous pour façonner l'avenir des jeux en ligne ! ENTER THE GAME 🎮 La verticale Turf de Betclic nourrit une ambition forte de croissance. Pour accompagner son développement, nous recherchons un(e) stagiaire en marketing opérationnel , qui contribuera à coordonner les actions marketing dédiées aux courses hippiques : acquisition, affiliation, sponsoring, réseaux sociaux, CRM… Vous travaillerez avec les équipes Marketing, Produit, Tech et Data, au croisement du sport, du digital et des paris en ligne. YOUR ROLE WITHIN BETCLIC 🔥 Aux côtés de l’équipe Turf, vous participerez à la préparation, au suivi et à l’analyse des actions marketing de la verticale. Vous contribuerez également à animer les partenariats liés à l’univers hippique et à améliorer la coordination entre les équipes internes et les partenaires. Ce stage vous permettra de découvrir concrètement le fonctionnement d’une activité digitale dans l’univers des paris sportifs. Parmi les missions : Contribuer à la coordination des actions marketing de la verticale Turf avec les équipes internes. Participer au suivi des campagnes et à l’analyse de leur performance. Aider à identifier des pistes d’amélioration à partir des retours utilisateurs et des résultats observés. Participer à la réflexion sur l’évolution de l’expérience Turf, notamment sur le produit et le mobile. Contribuer à la veille sur les usages digitaux, l’IA et les tendances du secteur. Prendre part au suivi opérationnel des partenariats de la verticale. WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? 🔍 Nous recherchons un(e) étudiant(e) en Master 1 ou Master 2, curieux(se) et motivé(e) par les univers du digital, de la tech et des paris sportifs. Une appétence pour le Turf serait un vrai plus, sans être indispensable. Il est fait pour vous si : Vous préparez un diplôme de niveau Master, idéalement en marketing, digital, communication, commerce ou gestion de projet. Vous vous intéressez à la tech, aux produits digitaux et aux nouveaux usages, notamment sur mobile. Vous êtes curieux(se) des paris sportifs et souhaitez découvrir les spécificités de ce secteur. Vous avez un intérêt pour l’IA et ses applications concrètes, et vous appréciez suivre les performances des actions mises en place. Vous aimez organiser et coordonner des sujets, et savez avancer avec méthode. Vous appréciez les échanges avec des interlocuteurs variés et le travail en équipe. Vous savez prendre des initiatives et n’hésitez pas à poser des questions pour progresser. WHAT ARE THE RECRUITMENT STEPS? 📝 - Si votre candidature est retenue, Benoît vous contactera sous une semaine pour un premier échange RH (30 minutes). - Vous passerez ensuite un entretien plus approfondi avec Julien (Directeur Turf) et Alexis (Lead Product Owner Turf) - Vous réaliserez le test AssessFirst (personnalité, motivation et raisonnement cognitif). - Enfin, Benoit mènera un dernier entretien RH pour passer en revue vos résultats au test AssessFirst. Le processus de recrutement dure généralement entre 4 et 6 semaines afin de vous garantir une expérience optimale. WHAT CAN YOU EXPECT? 🎁 🍽️ Une carte Ticket Restaurant® créditée de 11 € par jour (dont 6 € pris en charge par Betclic) 🚆 Remboursement à 50 % des frais de transports en commun ou une prime annuelle de mobilité durable (230 € pour les trajets domicile-travail en mode de transport durable) 🏡 Un modèle de travail hybride remote / présentiel 🏢 Des bureaux exceptionnels dotés d'un rooftop pour profiter de pauses ensoleillées avec vue sur la Cité du Vin 🎉 Des événements internes pour rythmer votre quotidien 🏋️ Des cours de sport sur site et des tournois organisés (Pilates, circuit training, boxe, yoga, futsal, padel, tennis…) Stage rémunéré de 6 mois, à partir de Janvier 2027, à Bordeaux. Un contrat d’apprentissage n’est pas envisageable pour ce poste. 📍 Groupe Betclic – 117 Quai de Bacalan, 33300 BORDEAUX

items.title: Digital Campaigns, Policy Advocacy
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We're hiring a strategist to join the Policy Campaigns team within Anthropic's Public Policy team. The Policy Campaigns team turns the company's policy priorities into active campaigns: research and polling, messaging, coalitions, paid media, and external execution. We're hiring a strategist to develop and execute paid media campaign strategy, manage agencies, and measure the success of our advocacy campaigns in the US and in priority markets abroad. This is a strategy and program management role. You'll decide what a campaign needs to accomplish, who needs to hear from us, which messages and tactics will move them, and then implement accordingly. Anthropic works on many policy issues at once, across many markets, and you'll need to understand the full set of issues and find the right cross-cutting approaches to advance our goals. You'll direct the agencies that produce and place the work, and bring Policy, Communications, Marketing, Public Affairs, and Legal to agreement on tight legislative timelines. The role also carries a substantial project management load. You'll run several campaigns at once, across time zones and agencies, and keep each one on schedule and on budget. You'll report to the Head of Policy Campaigns. Key responsibilities Design paid and digital campaign strategies for legislative and policy goals, including objectives, audiences, messaging, tactics, phasing, and budget Develop campaign messaging and tactics with the Campaigns team, executives, Public Affairs, and Communications, and make sure paid media carries the core message Spot where a campaign could conflict with Anthropic's other policy, commercial, or international priorities, and resolve those tensions before launch Direct creative and media-buying agencies: set strategy and briefs, scopes and budgets, hold timelines, and hold the work to a high standard Run several campaigns at once across time zones and agencies: own the timelines, workplans, budgets, and status reporting, and keep partners in the US and abroad aligned Build rapid response capabilities with Policy, Marketing, Legal, and Communications so campaigns can respond quickly in changing environments Set success measures before launch, report results plainly, and adjust strategy based on what works Work cross-functionally to find the stories and moments that make policy arguments concrete for policymakers and opinion formers Minimum qualifications Experience running digital content and paid media for a corporate affairs team, political campaign, advocacy organization, public affairs firm, or issue campaign, including owning a media budget Experience managing creative and media-buying agencies, including briefs, scopes, budgets, and performance reviews Experience running campaigns aimed at policymakers, key opinion formers, or other influential audiences Experience managing several campaigns or projects at once, with multiple agencies and stakeholders in different time zones Experience building campaign reporting in spreadsheets or dashboards Preferred qualifications Experience managing state or federal legislative campaigns Experience running campaigns inside a large organization or coalition with competing priorities Working knowledge of AI safety and technology policy issues Experience running campaigns in markets outside the US Hands-on familiarity with ad platforms and targeting, such as Meta, LinkedIn, and programmatic buying The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $265,000 — $295,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Senior Director Business Operations
items.description: ABOUT POLYMARKET Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future. We're growing fast, both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire. ABOUT THE ROLE Polymarket is growing fast and the operational infrastructure hasn't kept pace. This role exists to fix that. You'll sit at the center of the business, working directly with executive leadership to turn strategy into execution across every function. That means owning the planning cycles, the metrics, the cross-functional programs, and the hard conversations about what gets prioritized and what doesn't. This is not a support role. You'll be expected to have opinions, make calls, and drive outcomes. The BizOps team is small and the scope is large. You'll be building the operating model as much as running it, which means a lot of the work is zero-to-one. There's no established playbook for most of what Polymarket is doing, and this role is responsible for writing it. If you've spent your career in environments where the processes already exist, this will be an adjustment. If you've built them before and want to do it again at a company with real scale and momentum, this is the job. The person who succeeds here will be someone who can hold complexity across multiple workstreams without losing the thread, who earns trust from functional leaders by being useful rather than by having authority, and who can move between a board-level strategy memo and a messy operational problem in the same week. The mandate is broad by design. Polymarket needs an operator who can figure out what the business needs and go build it. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the annual and quarterly planning cycles, including OKR-setting, long-range planning, and quarterly business reviews with exec and functional leadership - Run weekly and monthly business reviews, building the dashboards, scorecards, and reporting infrastructure leadership uses to track performance and make decisions - Scope and stand up net-new initiatives that don't yet have a clear owner, from new market entry to partnership structures to internal pilots, and see them through to operational handoff - Act as the connective tissue across product, engineering, sales, marketing, and finance on programs where no single function owns the outcome end-to-end - Unblock stalled cross-functional work by diagnosing root causes, resolving prioritization conflicts, and driving decisions when teams are stuck - Prepare briefing documents, decision memos, and exec and board materials that give leadership what they need to make high-stakes calls quickly - Identify operational inefficiencies across the business and build the playbooks and processes that make execution less dependent on tribal knowledge WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 10+ years of experience in BizOps, Strategy and Operations, or a Chief of Staff function, with at least 3 years in a leadership role managing teams or programs at significant scale - Demonstrated track record of building cross-functional operating processes from scratch, including planning cycles, business reviews, and metrics infrastructure - Strong analytical foundation, including experience with forecasting, unit economics, cohort analysis, and variance analysis against plan, with fluency in SQL or a willingness to get there fast - Experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder programs where you had influence but not direct authority over the people doing the work - Clear, structured written communication, you can write a tight decision memo or a board slide that doesn't need a verbal explanation to land - Comfortable operating in ambiguity, you've been handed problems with no existing owner before and know how to scope them before you solve them - (Plus) Experience at a high-growth technology company or marketplace business, especially one operating in a regulated or novel industry - (Plus) Exposure to financial products, trading platforms, or consumer applications with real-time data and complex user behavior BENEFITS - Competitive salary & equity - Unlimited PTO - Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage - 401k match - Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories PAY TRANSPARENCY Base salary range: $350,000 to $450,000, plus equity and benefits. This is a good-faith range for the level we're hiring at. Experience varies widely within a title here, so if your expectations fall outside it, reach out anyway. We're always happy to talk it through.

items.location_text: US - Remote, New York City, Seattle, Washington, DC, San Francisco
items.description: About the Team OpenAI builds powerful AI systems like ChatGPT, the OpenAI API, and enterprise products that serve millions of users across the globe. As we scale, securing our infrastructure, protecting sensitive data, supporting employees’ velocity, and meeting global compliance standards are essential to our success and societal impact. Security at OpenAI is a cross-cutting organization that includes Security, Privacy, IT, GRC, Corporate Security, and other teams. Program Managers play a critical role in aligning teams and delivering execution at scale. About the Role We’re seeking a Program Manager to build and own programs that span OpenAI’s Security organization, with a core focus on Mergers & Acquisitions. You will work across domains from diligence through Day 1 readiness, integration, onboarding, and transition to ongoing ownership. You will also apply what you build to other priorities that span Security teams. You will learn how work actually moves between teams, spot gaps and unclear ownership, and build practical systems that make complex transitions easier to execute. This role is deeply cross-functional and execution-focused. It requires a structured operator who thrives in ambiguity, partners effectively across boundaries, and applies principled judgment to drive programs at speed from initial planning through durable handoff. You will use AI and automation to reduce repetitive work and help teams operate at greater scale, while applying sound judgment to sensitive information and consequential decisions. In this role, you will: - Own Security & IT M&A programs, including supporting System Operations and other engineering teams in defining and performing timely diligence assessments, and scoping, planning, and executing acquisition integrations. Carry the work through Day 1 readiness, onboarding of people and systems, post-close priorities, and handoff to ongoing owners. - Partner with Corporate Development, IT, Infrastructure, Application, Legal, Privacy, Security, GRC, Corporate Security and other teams to understand cross-functional requirements and navigate tradeoffs. Make responsibilities and decision rights clear while bringing in the right experts for technical and risk judgments. - Learn partner teams’ workflows and identify missed dependencies, bottlenecks, duplicated effort, and risks that could slow an integration or weaken its outcome. Address recurring problems at their source. - Establish scalable frameworks and processes to support core programs, including defining durable program goals and core measures of success. Build useful intake paths, playbooks, onboarding checklists, decision points, and handoff standards that teams adopt in practice. - Use AI and automation to organize information, surface gaps, improve documentation, route work, and track follow-through, with appropriate handling of sensitive information and human review of risk decisions. - Create and maintain program-level visibility across deals, risks, milestones, and dependencies, ensuring program outcomes are delivered reliably and at high quality. Measure whether the work improves readiness, reduces manual effort, closes risks, and makes future transitions more predictable. - Communicate status, risks, tradeoffs, and decisions clearly to technical and executive audiences and drive cross-functional execution with urgency and care. - Own additional programs that span Security and IT as organizational priorities evolve, applying and improving the systems built through the M&A portfolio. You might thrive in this role if you: - Are an empathetic communicator and leader who is able to influence a variety of cross-functional and executive audiences, and build durable trust with partners. - Have 5+ years of experience leading complex cross-functional programs, with a proven record of successful partnership in security, IT, infrastructure, privacy, trust, product risk, or other technical domains. - Have carried programs from an ambiguous starting point through execution and lasting ownership. - Have built a new program, workflow, or operating model yourself and can show how you earned adoption and improved results. - Are curious about how teams work in practice and can find the underlying issue behind a missed handoff or recurring exception. - Have used AI or automation to improve a real workflow and can explain what changed, how people adopted it, and where human judgment remains necessary. - Have experience in Mergers & Acquisitions or related areas. - Thrive in high-trust environments, bring rigor and systems thinking to ambiguity, and operate with a bias for aligned execution over org boundaries. - Are structured, detail-oriented, and rigorous in ensuring quality, accountability, and durable delivery. items.title: Dedicated Support Engineer - San Francisco
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises. About the Role The Support Engineering team works closely with Engineering, Product, Technical Success, Go-to-Market, and other teams to deliver an exceptional experience for our most strategic customers. We combine deep technical troubleshooting with durable customer context, proactive reliability work, and clear ownership during critical moments. We use automation, agents, and our own technology to help build the future of technical support. We’re looking for experienced, deeply curious technical problem-solvers to serve as trusted support partners for our Premium Support customers. You’ll work directly with customers on novel, ambiguous, and high-impact technical issues, using logs, telemetry, reproduction, and systems-level investigation to isolate causes and drive issues toward resolution. Beyond resolving individual issues, you’ll use your deep understanding of OpenAI’s infrastructure and products, together with each customer’s architecture and operating context, to anticipate risk and make their workloads more resilient over time. You’ll proactively monitor integrations, identify emerging failure patterns and architectural breakpoints, and work with customers and internal teams to address them before they become incidents. Success means that as a customer’s workloads mature and scale, the day-to-day effort required to support them decreases through better monitoring, runbooks, automation, and preventative improvements. In this role, you will: - Work directly with Premium Support customers to troubleshoot their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, unexpected product behavior, performance degradation, and production incidents. - Provide end-to-end technical ownership by analyzing logs and system behavior, reproducing errors, testing hypotheses, and isolating the likely failure domain. Where possible, you’ll identify the root cause before escalating to Engineering; where that is not possible, you’ll provide a clear hypothesis and the evidence needed to accelerate Engineering’s investigation. - Become a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and systems, serving as a critical escalation point and a technical backstop for our most strategic customers. - Own the customer-specific response to high-impact incidents. You’ll assess severity and business impact, initiate the appropriate response path, coordinate cross-functional responders, maintain clear ownership, and ensure issues move through mitigation, resolution, and post-incident follow-through. - Communicate clearly and proactively during periods of uncertainty, providing accurate updates to customer technical teams, business stakeholders, executives, and internal partners. - Develop a detailed understanding of each customer’s architecture, integrations, dependencies, critical workloads, and operational constraints. You’ll document this context and make it accessible to Support, Product, and Engineering teams. - Partner with Go-to-Market and Technical Success teams to understand the business importance of customer workloads and ensure that relevant commercial context informs severity, prioritization, and communication without bypassing established support processes. - Represent Support Engineering in relevant customer meetings, including QBRs, and partner closely with account teams to communicate technical health, surface risks and blockers early, coordinate follow-up, and provide customers and internal stakeholders with clear, proactive updates. - Monitor customer integrations and support trends to identify emerging risks, recurring failure patterns, and readiness gaps before they become major escalations. - Prepare for important launches, migrations, traffic increases, and business events by developing account-specific runbooks, validating escalation paths, coordinating support readiness, and providing heightened monitoring where needed. - Lead or contribute to incident reviews and postmortems, identify opportunities to prevent recurrence, and track corrective actions through closure. - Translate recurring customer pain into clear, evidence-backed feedback for Product and Engineering, with a particular focus on improving the reliability and performance of existing products, integrations, and deployments. - Turn what you learn from customer investigations into scalable improvements, including troubleshooting guides, monitoring, internal tooling, support workflows, and AI-powered automation. - Help shape the operating model, technical standards, and tooling for Premium Support as the function grows globally. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have significant experience in Support Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or another role involving hands-on diagnosis of complex production issues. - Have expert-level troubleshooting skills and a strong track record of resolving ambiguous technical problems across APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise integrations. - Are comfortable working with logs, metrics, traces, API requests, authentication flows, and customer-provided code or configurations to understand system behavior and test hypotheses. - Have experience leading or playing a central role in customer-impacting incidents, including severity assessment, technical coordination, stakeholder communication, root-cause analysis, and post-incident follow-through. - Can write code or scripts to reproduce issues, interrogate systems, automate repetitive work, and improve internal tools. Experience with Python, JavaScript, or similar languages is valuable. - Can communicate complex technical issues clearly to engineers, customer technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior leaders—especially when information is incomplete or evolving. - Build strong, high-trust relationships with customers and cross-functional partners while maintaining clear and scalable ownership boundaries. - Look beyond the immediate issue to identify patterns, improve the system, and prevent the same problem from recurring. - Thrive in ambiguity, update quickly as new information emerges, and are willing to learn whatever is needed to get the job done. - Bring a humble, team-first mindset, strong judgment, and a genuine eagerness to help both customers and colleagues succeed. - Are excited to use OpenAI’s products, agents, and emerging AI capabilities to transform how technical support operates at scale. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form https://form.asana.com/?d=57018692298241&k=5MqR40fZd7jlxVUh5J-UeA. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link https://form.asana.com/?k=bQ7w9h3iexRlicUdWRiwvg&d=57018692298241. items.title: Global Mobility Lead
items.description: ABOUT THE JOB We're looking for an experienced Global Mobility Lead to build and run the programs that help employees join, move, and work across borders. You will own our mobility policies, immigration casework, and vendor relationships, and partner with Legal, Finance, and People Ops to make cross-border moves clear, compliant, and well supported. WHAT YOU’LL OWN GLOBAL MOBILITY - Own the mobility policy suite end to end: relocation, permanent transfers, short-term and long-term international assignments, remote/cross-border work arrangements, and business travel thresholds. - Run individual mobility cases from scoping to landing: package design, cost estimates, immigration sequencing, tax and social-security implications, payroll setup, relocation logistics, and post-arrival support. - Manage employment-based immigration casework in partnership with outside counsel: H-1B (including cap-subject and change-of-employer/AC21 timing), L-1, TN, E-3, O-1, F-1 OPT/CPT, and employer-sponsored permanent residence. Own the internal timeline, the start-date reality check, and the manager/candidate communication. - Own daily immigration intake and case execution, including employer questionnaires, supporting documents, employment verification letters, signatures, counsel follow ups, and case closure. - Own right-to-work compliance across jurisdictions: I-9 and E-Verify in the US, Home Office share-code checks in the UK, and equivalent checks in our EU and other markets. - Decide and document the entity/employment model for each new market (direct entity, EOR, or non-resident payroll registration) with Finance and Legal. - Own our mobility vendor stack (immigration counsel, relocation, tax, EOR/global payroll): scope, SLAs, cost, and performance. - Model and track mobility cost, including sponsorship and premium-processing fees, so leadership can make go/no-go calls with real numbers, and obtain and document required approvals before committing sponsorship or spend DATA AND SYSTEMS - Build the tracking layer: mobility case pipeline, immigration deadlines and expirations, compensation comparisons, etc. - Stand up mobility dashboards: case volume, cycle time, cost per move, band penetration, offer-to-band variance, and equity-gap trend. - Write the employee-facing documentation so moves and pay decisions are predictable and explainable, not one-off negotiations. What we’re looking for REQUIRED - 6+ years of experience in global mobility, with real ownership of cross-border moves and immigration casework, not just vendor hand-offs. - Working fluency in US employment-based immigration and at least one other major jurisdiction’s work-authorization regime (UK, EU, or Canada). - Strong analytical skills: comfortable in spreadsheets and HRIS reporting, able to build a defensible model and explain the assumptions behind it. - Judgment about risk. You know when to escalate to Legal, when to flag classification or permanent-establishment exposure, and how to say no clearly. - Excellent written communication: you’ll draft policies, verification letters, offer rationales, and executive-facing recommendations. - Comfort with ambiguity, high volume, and shifting priorities.

items.title: Director, Government Relations (APAC)
items.description: About Us Fanatics is building a leading global digital sports platform. We ignite the passions of global sports fans and maximize the presence and reach for our hundreds of sports partners globally by offering products and services across Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, and Fanatics Betting & Gaming, allowing sports fans to Buy, Collect, and Bet. Through the Fanatics platform, sports fans can buy licensed fan gear, jerseys, lifestyle and streetwear products, headwear, and hardgoods; collect physical and digital trading cards, sports memorabilia, and other digital assets; and bet as the company builds its Sportsbook and iGaming platform. Fanatics has an established database of over 100 million global sports fans; a global partner network with approximately 900 sports properties, including major national and international professional sports leagues, players associations, teams, colleges, college conferences and retail partners, 2,500 athletes and celebrities, and 200 exclusive athletes; and over 2,000 retail locations, including its Lids retail stores. Our more than 22,000 employees are committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience and delighting sports fans globally. The Role As the Director of Government Relations at Fanatics, APAC, you work closely with our leadership team to ensure we remain at the forefront of legislative trends and industry developments, across the Asia-Pacific region, with an initial focus on Japan and China. In this role, you will provide strategic insights, advocate for our interests, and drive initiatives that reflect Fanatics' commitment to innovation, consumer satisfaction, and the evolving retail landscape. What You’ll Do: Forge and Maintain Strategic Relationships: Cultivate and sustain high-impact relationships with key government officials and policymakers across the APAC region, with an initial focus on Japan and China—including members of the Japanese Diet, government ministries and agencies, as well as senior officials at both central and local government levels in China, regulatory authorities and other relevant policymakers—to advance Fanatics’ priorities. Provide Executive-Level Legislative Intelligence: Keep Fanatics leadership informed with timely, in-depth analyses of current and proposed legislation affecting the retail, sports, sports betting, and e-commerce sectors across key APAC markets, ensuring proactive and informed decision-making. Shape Policy and Drive Advocacy: Monitor the legislative and regulatory landscape across the APAC region, assess potential business impacts, and develop tailored, forward-thinking strategies that position Fanatics for success. Craft Persuasive Policy Communications: Develop compelling policy documents, including executive summaries, position papers, and advocacy briefs, that clearly articulate Fanatics’ policy positions to key stakeholders. Lead Cross-Functional Collaboration: Manage external consultants, engage internal stakeholders, and oversee special projects that align with and advance Fanatics’ policy and business objectives. Advocate with Authority: Present Fanatics’ policy positions to government officials, trade associations, coalitions, and industry stakeholders, across the APAC region, ensuring alignment between corporate priorities and broader legislative and market trends. Strengthen Industry Influence: Enhance partnerships with trade associations, advocacy groups, and community organizations, reinforcing Fanatics' role as a thought leader in the retail and sports ecosystem. Innovate and Push Boundaries: Develop and execute creative advocacy strategies that challenge the status quo and unlock new opportunities for Fanatics in a rapidly evolving regulatory environment. Showcase Fanatics’ Impact: Organize immersive site visits, retail events, and media engagements for elected officials to deepen their understanding of Fanatics’ business model, innovation, and community contributions. What We’re Looking For: Policy Expertise & Thought Leadership: Deep understanding of public policy, with the ability to distill complex regulatory issues into clear, actionable insights. Extensive Experience: 10+ years of relevant experience in government, public policy or government affairs, including experience working in government, parliament, public administration or regulatory authorities and/or in government affairs roles within companies, trade associations or public affairs consultancies. APAC Expertise: Strong knowledge and understanding of the political, legislative and regulatory environments across the APAC region, particularly in Japan and China. Language Skills: Fluency in English, Japanese and Mandarin Chinese is required. Political Acumen & Agility: Highly adaptable, with the ability to anticipate and respond to shifting political and regulatory landscapes. Compelling Communicator: Exceptional writing, presentation, and interpersonal skills to effectively articulate Fanatics' policy positions and influence diverse audiences. Master Negotiator & Influencer: Proven ability to navigate complex policy challenges, persuade stakeholders, and drive favorable outcomes. Strategic & Innovative Problem Solver: A visionary approach to advocacy, with the ability to develop creative solutions that advance Fanatics' objectives. Proven Leadership & Execution: Demonstrated success in leading teams and managing projects from strategy development through execution. Self-Starter with a Collaborative Mindset: Highly motivated, able to work independently while fostering cross-functional collaboration to drive impact. Storytelling & Brand Amplification: Passion for shaping and elevating the corporate narrative through strategic communications. Unwavering Integrity & Professionalism: Commitment to the highest ethical standards, confidentiality, and professional excellence. By submitting your application, you agree to our terms of service and acknowledge you have read our Candidate Privacy Policy. Fanatics will never ask candidates for money, banking information, or other sensitive personal information as part of the interview process. If you receive a suspicious message claiming to be from Fanatics recruiting, please do not respond and report it here .
